subject: PO acceptance, invoice cadence, and payment-holdback for CareCo pilot
messages:
From: Emily Song <emily.song@carecohealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@carecohealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO requirements and invoice cadence for Redwood pilot

Hi Jonas,

We are preparing a Purchase Order to start the pilot with Redwood. A few procurement constraints to confirm before we submit the PO:

- Our standard is monthly consolidated invoices with Net 60 payment terms.
- For this supplier class we are required to hold 10% of each invoice for 90 days as a payment holdback (gov vendor rule).
- PO must include the Redwood account number, remit-to, and our internal GL codes.

Could you confirm Redwood can accept Net 60 and the 10% holdback? If not, list the minimal alternate legal/finance language we'd need to include on the PO. We will attach the draft PO once the terms are agreed.

Attachments: CareCo_PO_8342.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Emily Song
Procurement Manager
CareCo Health
emily.song@carecohealth.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Song <emily.song@carecohealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements and invoice cadence for Redwood pilot

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear summary. We want to get the pilot started quickly; a few items from our side:

- Net terms: Redwood default is Net 30. We can operationally support Net 60 but will need to confirm credit and AR workflow with finance.
- Holdback: 10% holdback is outside our standard. Finance typically accepts up to 5% holdback with Legal sign-off. Could you share whether the holdback is applied to each invoice or only on milestone/final settlement?
- PO fields: Please include: Redwood account ID (we'll provide), remit-to (ACH/wiring details), billing contact, and a single referenced rate card line.

I'm attaching our current rate card and a brief PO acceptance checklist so procurement can map fields. If CareCo needs Net 60 + 10% holdback, we'll need an exception from Finance + a short amendment describing how the holdback will be released (e.g., escrow or applied against final invoice).

Proposed short path: if CareCo accepts a 5% holdback instead of 10%, Redwood will accept Net 60 with monthly consolidated invoices and no additional prepayment. If CareCo requires full 10% we will route to Legal/Finance for review and escalate.

Attachments: rate_card_redwood_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), PO_acceptance_checklist.txt (text/plain)

Can you send the redlined PO back and indicate whether the holdback is per-invoice or milestone-based?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements and invoice cadence for Redwood pilot — finance constraints

Jonas / team,

Quick finance note so we have clear constraints before we promise anything to the customer:

1) Holdback: Finance will not accept a >5% holdback without Legal approval. A 10% mandatory holdback triggers a credit / escrow mechanism and will require a contract addendum.
2) Net 60: We can support Net 60 for strategic cohorts with credit approval; if we move to Net 60, we ask for monthly consolidated invoices (single statement) and an early-pay discount option to preserve cash flow.
3) ERP mapping: Procurement must provide PO with BLANKET GL code(s), billing address, and remit-to. We also require supplier tax form and vendor setup lead time (usually 5–7 business days).

If Procurement must have 10% holdback, options: (a) accept 10% in escrow (requires legal + platform to track), (b) accept 5% at invoicing and negotiate remaining 5% off the final settlement after 90 days. Option (b) is operationally easiest.

I'm attaching a sample invoice header we need for vendor setup.

Attachments: sample_invoice_header.csv (text/csv)

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
From: Emily Song <emily.song@carecohealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@carecohealth.com
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements and invoice cadence for Redwood pilot — updated PO attached

Thanks for the fast responses. A few clarifications from Procurement:

- The 10% holdback is mandatory for this supplier class and will be applied per monthly invoice. It cannot be applied only at final settlement.
- We are able to provide monthly consolidated invoices and all required PO fields.
- CareCo is requesting a one-time onboarding credit of 15% on the first quarter to offset integration and security review costs.

We attached an updated PO (v2) that contains the GL mappings and billing address. Procurement needs final acceptance (or an escalation plan) by close of business Friday so we can route the PO internally.

Attachments: CareCo_PO_8342_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

Appreciate the collaboration — Emily
Emily Song
Procurement Manager
CareCo Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Song <emily.song@carecohealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, procurement@carecohealth.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements and invoice cadence for Redwood pilot — acceptance with conditions

Emily — thanks for the updated PO and the clear timeline. After internal review we can accept a commercial pathway to get the pilot moving with the following conditions:

1) Net 60 with monthly consolidated invoices: ACCEPTED (Finance-approved for this cohort).
2) Holdback: Redwood can accept a 5% per-invoice holdback operationally. We cannot accept 10% without Legal approval and an escrow mechanism. If CareCo requires full 10%, please sign the PO with the 10% term and we will route to Legal immediately; that will add ~7–10 business days.
3) Onboarding credit: Redwood will apply a one-time 10% onboarding credit (not 15%) on the first quarter invoices if CareCo signs a 12-month minimum commitment.

If CareCo is able to reduce the holdback to 5% and accept the 12-month commitment for the 10% onboarding credit, we will countersign the PO today and provide a DocuSign link. Otherwise, we'll escalate internally on Monday to Legal for the 10% request.

Attachments: accepted_po_stub.pdf (application/pdf)
Links: https://app.redwood.example/docusign/8342

Please let me know decision by EOD Friday and we'll action.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
